solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Government, in disarray, isn't being held in high regard

indicators.note: something in disarray is jumbled, so the letters of the next word are put in a new order
something held in sits inside a larger thing, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: high regard for someone is admiration
the letters of isn't, rearranged

explanation.surface: A government in chaos has lost the public's respect.
explanation.definitionFit: The administration is the governing body currently in office, the government of the day.

clue.text: Advent calendar finally included by a competitor

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, keeping only its closing letter
a thing included by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a rival is a competitor
the last letter of calendar

explanation.surface: A competitor turns up with an Advent calendar at the end of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advent calendar' reads as one thing, but Advent is the definition and calendar only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means a coming or arrival, the sense behind the Christian season's name.

clue.text: Does extra work on a tuneful arrangement, initially — work for pianists

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each of the words before it, keeping only their opening letters

blocks.note: to moonlight is to take a second job on the side
taken as written
taken as written
the first letters of tuneful and arrangement

explanation.surface: A musician takes on extra arranging work for pianists.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata is a famous piano sonata.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moonlight Sonata is a Beethoven piano piece, so a musical composition played by pianists.

clue.text: In the last resort, ultimately cleared of charges

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word in the phrase gives up only its final letter

blocks.note: the last letters of In, the, last and resort

explanation.surface: As a last resort, someone is finally cleared of criminal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests a courtroom, but here it means deductions such as fees or tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A nett sum is what remains after all deductions, fees and taxes have been taken off.

clue.text: With thoroughfare restricted, go on horseback or walk

blocks.note: a street, shortened to its standard abbreviation
to ride is to go on horseback

explanation.surface: With the road closed, the choice is to ride or walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, and to stride is to walk with long steps.

clue.text: Possibility of help or rescue at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble at sea hopes for help or a rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a supply or means of support that can be drawn on when needed.

clue.text: Mad Hatter I mostly describe as overdramatic

indicators.note: mad means crazed or disordered, so the letters that follow are scrambled
mostly means not all of it, so the word after loses its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to call something a name is to describe it as such

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland is called a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad Hatter' reads as Lewis Carroll's character, but Mad is the anagram signal for Hatter plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is exaggerated and showy, as though put on for a stage audience.

clue.text: Testing event for student looking down in the mouth?

blocks.note: first meaning: a spoken test, as in a viva or language exam
second meaning, read literally: a dentist peering into someone's mouth

explanation.surface: A student looks miserable at a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down in the mouth' means glum, but taken literally it is someone looking into a mouth, as a dentist does.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken exam is assessed by talking, while a dental check-up is literally an inspection of the mouth.

clue.text: One insect or another let out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: another insect, read from the clue's own insect: a bee
the letters of let, rearranged

explanation.surface: One insect or another is released from a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' leans on the definition's insect: another insect is a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a hard-winged insect, one of the largest orders of bugs.

clue.text: List including duck and domestic fowl

indicators.note: a thing including another holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a roster is a list of duties or names
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A farmyard inventory of ducks and hens.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, which gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, a farmyard bird kept domestically.

clue.text: Consult part of manual, say, for problem with tank

blocks.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
a page is one part of a manual

explanation.surface: Look up the right page in the handbook to fix a fault with the tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow leaking of liquid, a typical fault in a water or fuel tank.

clue.text: Component of evil empire that is particularly so

definitions.note: so refers back to evil: something particularly evil

indicators.note: a component is one part of a larger whole, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Part of an evil empire is the very worst of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue's own word 'evil': the answer is something especially wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile describes something extremely wicked or foul, so evil to a marked degree.

clue.text: Notice fair-minded people with little time producing change

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
just means fair, so fair-minded people are just men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Seeing fair people short of time leads someone to make an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a small alteration made to correct or improve something.

clue.text: Get animated about a distant island where big game can be watched

definitions.text: where big game can be watched

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps around the rest

blocks.note: to spark is to come alive or become lively
taken as written
far means distant
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited about a remote island where wild animals roam.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari park is a large enclosure where visitors drive among big wild animals such as lions.

clue.text: Preserve on record what prevents progress

indicators.note: one thing on another follows it in an across answer, so the second word is placed after

blocks.note: a log is a written record
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: Keeping something on the official record holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage, literally of floating timber, figuratively any deadlock that halts progress.

clue.text: Set off in vessel heading east after opening scenes

indicators.note: after says which piece comes first, putting the later-named one at the front

blocks.note: the first act of a play holds its opening scenes
a vat is a large vessel for liquid
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A ship sets out eastward after its first scenes, like a film opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a device or alarm is to trigger it, to set it off.

clue.text: Nice group of characters in sample, as anticipated

indicators.note: a group of characters inside these words is a run of consecutive letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A sample turns out nice, just as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' may suggest the French city, but it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or enjoyable, the everyday sense of nice.

clue.text: A Conservative supporter accepts workers' organisation, in fact

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so a piece is placed inside

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
TU is a trade union
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A Tory backer has really accepted the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade union is accepted not by the supporter alone but by the whole opening string, landing just after the Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually is an adverb meaning really, or as a matter of fact.

clue.text: Native growing up in mountainous area, possibly Nepali

definitions.text: Native growing up in mountainous area

indicators.note: possibly says the word could be arranged otherwise, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A person born and raised in the mountains, perhaps from Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' and 'growing up' suggest a person; the answer is a plant native to high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a plant that grows naturally in high mountain regions above the tree line.

clue.text: Communication devices run so long

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
adios is Spanish for goodbye, so long

explanation.surface: Phones or radios that keep running for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Radios are sets that send and receive signals, apparatus for communicating at a distance.

clue.text: Fish European river for sport

blocks.note: a snook is a sea fish
E is the abbreviation for European
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Angling in a European river as a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a verb about angling; here it is a noun naming a particular fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game played on a table, a recognised sport with professional players.

clue.text: A request received by US city or state

indicators.note: a thing received by another is taken into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A petition sent in to an American city or state government.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest of the fifty United States, in the far north-west.

clue.text: Endless difficulty framing suitable answer that's useful

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the following word loses its final letter
framing means surrounding like a picture frame, so the rest go inside

blocks.note: a problem is a difficulty
fit means suitable
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A hard problem turns out to have a handy, fitting solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profitable brings gain or benefit, so it is advantageous or worthwhile.

clue.text: Asian leader in past hiding yen in part of Ireland

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: Mao Zedong, former leader of China
Y is the symbol for yen

explanation.surface: A former Asian ruler stashing Japanese money somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Musicians not allowed in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the answer is what the phrase sounds like when heard

blocks.note: banned means forbidden, not allowed

explanation.surface: Players excluded from a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' fits the musical picture but is the homophone signal, since it literally means a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians who play together.

clue.text: Once more coming back over a river, one with spectacular views

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
again means once more

explanation.surface: Revisiting a river with fine scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string A, R, AGAIN is read backwards. Niagara is a river famous for its falls on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara, with its huge waterfalls, is visited chiefly for its dramatic scenery.

clue.text: Case is sorted out by king poorly, in the main

indicators.note: sorted out means rearranged, so the letters before it are put in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A case is handled badly by a king who feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seasick is feeling ill on board ship, unwell while out on the ocean.

clue.text: Standard variety of green trade for this kind of farmer

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of something, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: a mark is a standard, as in up to the mark
the letters of green and trade, rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer dealing in standard green produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A market gardener grows vegetables and fruit on a small scale for sale, a kind of small farmer.
